runConfig.positivePrompt: Static locked wide camera, one continuous five-second shot with no cuts. Preserve the attached approved still as the exact first-frame anatomy, identity, composition, lighting, and background reference. There are exactly two dinosaurs. The large dark grey horned quadruped filling the LEFT foreground is Triceratops. Freeze every pixel of that left Triceratops for the entire shot: its closed mouth, head, three horns, frill, torso, four feet, and tail never move or change. The smaller brown biped standing on the RIGHT background bank is Tyrannosaurus rex. Animate ONLY the head, short neck, throat, and lower jaw of that RIGHT brown Tyrannosaurus. Freeze its torso, pelvis, hips, both planted hind feet, toes, two tiny arms, and complete tail at their exact source coordinates. First, the RIGHT Tyrannosaurus holds still with its mouth closed. Next it makes one small controlled downward head nod of about five degrees without moving forward. Then it raises the head slightly and opens only its lower jaw smoothly in one direction to a moderate twenty-five-degree gape. The throat expands once and the final second holds the open-mouth silent roar. It never closes the jaw, returns, recoils, lunges, repeats, or reverses. Preserve the RIGHT Tyrannosaurus deep broad side-profile skull, stable teeth, low tongue, dark mouth interior, and uninterrupted neck attachment. Keep the stream visibly separating both dinosaurs. No contact, attack, injury, or panic. Silent, non-graphic generated display hypothesis for ages five to fourteen.
